correctness.rationale: For fixed admissible Lipschitz graphs the arclength densities are 1+O(ε²) a.e., so P=4+O(ε²), and replacing each sample by an equal branch choice and uniform x costs O(ε²) in the bounded expected distance. The limiting mean horizontal distance is 2/3. Independently of the exact kernel primitive, split the distance excess into |x−z|≤ε, contributing O(ε²) by bounded graph heights, and its complement. There the leading term is ε²(u(x)−v(z))²/(2|x−z|), with integrated Taylor remainder O(ε²) from ε⁴|x−z|⁻³. Same-branch squared differences are O(|x−z|²). For opposite branches, replacing the squared difference by h(x)² costs O(ε²) after integration by Lipschitz regularity. The z-integral of 1/|x−z| over the complement is 2log(1/ε) plus a function bounded in L¹(dx) by the integrable endpoint logarithms. Each cross integral therefore contributes ε²log(1/ε)∫h²; two ordered cross terms of weight 1/16 each followed by division by P→4 give 1/32. Strict Cauchy–Schwarz gives ∫h²>A²/2 because the endpoints vanish and the continuous profile is positive inside. The Dirichlet Green representation expresses h/A as an area-one tent mixture, each with squared norm 2/3. Strict convexity of the squared L² norm forces a single apex at equality. Concave height-rescaled plateaus with tip ramps shrinking to zero approach the lower bound. These yield exactly the claimed interval and equality statements.
residual_risks: The scope is fixed Lipschitz graph lenses and full-boundary Euclidean arclength sampling; the remainder need not be uniform in profile and no full ε² constant is claimed. A quadrature diagnostic cannot prove the asymptotic.

value.rationale: The global inequality leaves open how quickly and by what shape-dependent amount a collapsing lens approaches equality. This law isolates the singular scale and its coefficient for arbitrary fixed Lipschitz lenses, separates thickness from the midline, and turns a known width-moment envelope into an exact leading-deficit comparison at fixed unscaled area. It predicts more than specific symmetric or exactly integrable examples without claiming a new concavity inequality.
residual_risks: Only the leading logarithm is identified; no uniform stability lower bound, subsequent coefficient, or unbounded-slope extension is established.
